Resolves #17819

`Neo.component.Splitter` now supports opt-in live resizing without a cloned proxy or an App-Worker update per pointer frame. The existing DragZone registers a main-thread resize descriptor; `Neo.main.addon.DragDrop` delegates transient outer-wrapper geometry to one focused controller and sends a frozen axis/size/target tuple at release for one durable `wrapperStyle` commit. Proxy mode remains the default and retains commit-on-end behavior.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium pointer gestures, Neural Link worker-state inspection, buffered Grid/TreeGrid rendering, and exact Escape restoration) → L3 required (all close-target runtime ACs). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket

- The implementation pivoted from the ticket's first App-Worker-per-frame exploration to the operator-suggested main-thread `DragDrop` path. The ticket body was corrected in place before this PR.
- Main-thread resize state lives in `src/main/draggable/Resize.mjs`, keeping `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` at +31 lines over its 1,900-line baseline rather than adding another large responsibility block.
- Successful terminal commits carry the gesture-captured axis and outer target id, so reactive config churn cannot redirect a resize at release.
- Missing, removed, or stale target registrations fail closed. Escape, reset, unregister, and destruction restore the exact inline properties captured at gesture start.

- Splitter Neural Link journey: `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<Brain runtime> npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/core/SplitterLiveResizeNL.spec.mjs --workers=1` — 6 passed; live/deferred behavior, Escape, and vertical/horizontal × previous/next matrix.
- Heavy widget and wrapped-root surface: `SplitterHeavyContent.spec.mjs` — 2 passed; four alternating real drags across buffered Grid + TreeGrid plus a SplitButton outer-wrapper witness.
- Existing DockSplitter compatibility: `DockSplitterProxyPaintNL.spec.mjs` + `DockSplitterZoneIdNL.spec.mjs` — 3 passed; proxy paint and cold-boot first-gesture/Escape routing unchanged.
- Focused source/lifecycle suite after formatter pass: 46 passed across Splitter, DragZone, and DragDrop.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Commit `bbc3673949`: Engine's retained pre-commit hook passed whitespace, shorthand, JSDoc types, ticket archaeology, block alignment, parse, derived-domain, fixed-sleep, and Engine/Brain boundary guards.
- Post-split preflight note: Engine no longer exposes `npm run agent-preflight`; the Brain-runtime entrypoint performed alignment, capability/`feat` validation, and PR-body lint, while correctly refusing its repo-root-bound ticket-archaeology gate. The preceding Engine-native hook receipt covers that source gate in its owning repository.

## Evolution

The first no-proxy prototype proved live Flexbox resizing through App-Worker `drag:move`, including the heavy widget witness. The operator's main-thread observation exposed the stronger ownership boundary: pointer frames are physical presentation, while `wrapperStyle` is durable state. The final design therefore emits zero live move frames to the App Worker and performs one terminal VDOM commit.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-08-28T07:25:11Z

## Reviewer correction — the premise is frame budget, not ownership

Correcting my own review at [PRR_kwDODSospM8AAAABLO2UFA](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/17822#pullrequestreview-5048734740). The operator has confirmed the driver for the main-thread pivot was **performance**, not an architectural ownership boundary:

> it was not really about ownership boundaries, but performance. if we want a live-resize, worker roundtrips in the shape app -> vdom -> main -> app can cost us lags and missing frames.

My review's central framing — "pointer frames are physical presentation, `wrapperStyle` is durable state" — is a *description* of the resulting split, not the reason for it. I took that reason from the PR body's Evolution section and the ticket's Architectural Reality section, both author-written, which is precisely what guide §0 warns against: the PR's self-description is a claim to verify, not the premise. I verified the *what* rigorously and adopted the *why* uncritically. My §7.4 drift audit passed because framing matched mechanics — it could not catch that the framing itself had drifted from the motivation.

**The approval stands unchanged.** Nothing in this diff claims a frame budget, the mode is opt-in with the default `false`, and the change is correct on every axis I checked. But re-reading the evidence set under a performance premise surfaces one thing worth recording before the default is ever flipped.

### The eliminated roundtrip is the mechanism; frame cadence is the outcome, and it is unmeasured

What the witnesses prove, verified at `e5ebac2679`:

| Property | Measured? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Zero App-Worker move frames per pointer frame | **yes**, positive-controlled | `DragDrop.spec.mjs` — asserts `width === '220px'` before `sent.toEqual([])` |
| No geometry split-brain under buffered Grid + TreeGrid | **yes** | `SplitterHeavyContent.spec.mjs` — virtualized header/cell alignment, ≤3px return-to-boundary across four alternating drags |
| Transient frames never become durable worker state | **yes** | `SplitterLiveResizeNL.spec.mjs:114` |
| **Frame cadence / dropped frames / gesture latency** | **no** | nothing — every `toBeLessThan*` in both witnesses is a pixel tolerance, not a duration. No `performance.now()`, no rAF counting, no elapsed-time or budget assertion anywhere in the added specs |

Removing an `app → vdom → main → app` hop per pointer frame is the single largest win available here, so the prior is strongly favourable — this is not a suspicion that live mode is slow. It is that the property the architecture was chosen *for* has no witness, while the property it produces as a side effect has three.

That matters for one specific downstream decision. #17819 states that "the real Grid/TreeGrid witness decides whether the mode is ready beyond opt-in use". Under an ownership premise that reads fine — correctness under heavy widgets is the question. Under the actual performance premise, **the gate on flipping the default does not measure the property the default flip depends on.** Correctness under load and cadence under load are different measurements, and only the first exists.

Not a required action and not a follow-up on this PR — the ACs as written are met and the default is unchanged. Recording it so that whoever proposes `liveResize: true` as the default inherits an accurate gate rather than a green suite that never looked at timing. The same correction applies to #17820's dock preview and to D#17818's edge-resize contract, where I endorsed the same ownership framing; I am carrying it there.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** Ticket #17819 in full (ACs, Contract Ledger, Out of Scope, Avoided Traps); the changed-file list; `origin/dev` source of `Splitter.mjs`, `DragZone.mjs`, `DragDrop.mjs`, `DomAccess.mjs`, `DockSplitter.mjs`; sibling precedent in `src/main/draggable/sensor/`; `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` on dev; PR #16797's eager-registration invariant as cited by the ticket; and a Memory Core prior-art sweep that surfaced your two pre-implementation audits plus the operator's mid-implementation architectural correction.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Live mode should keep per-frame geometry on the main thread and commit durable layout exactly once at release through the worker-owned `wrapperStyle`, with the proxy path untouched by default. It must **not** hardcode a second gesture system beneath `DragDrop`, must **not** let a generic `src/component` primitive acquire dock- or app-specific assumptions, and must freeze the commit target at gesture start so reactive config churn cannot redirect it. Test isolation should include proxy-mode regression coverage, a heavy buffered-widget witness, and an assertion that no move frame reaches the App Worker.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Improves** on the expected shape. Two things exceeded it. First, `Resize.finish()` deliberately does not revert on success while `cancel()` restores captured properties *with their original priority* — a distinction I expected to have to ask for. Second, `apply()` computes terminal size identically in both modes and only gates the DOM write on `preview`, so deferred mode inherits the frozen-tuple math instead of the old asynchronous parent measurement. What changed my premise concretely: I arrived expecting to argue that transient main-thread inline styles would desynchronise from worker state, and `applyResize` writes **both** `flex: 'none'` and `[axis]` into `wrapperStyle` (`src/component/Splitter.mjs:120-124`), exactly the pair `Resize.apply()` sets inline. There is no worker-unknown orphan property, so the split-brain I came to look for cannot form.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres — verify-before-assert. The ticket's own Avoided Traps names "Claiming performance by architecture: the buffered-widget browser witness remains the proof", and the PR did not claim the default should flip; `liveResize` stays `false` and the heavy Grid/TreeGrid witness is what would license any future change. ### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` `setConfigs` makes two non-obvious choices with no in-line rationale, inside the 1,900-line file this PR is otherwise careful to keep thin:

```js
DragDrop.prototype.registerZone.call(me, data);
delete data.resizeConfig;
```

Neither is self-explaining. `prototype.call` instead of `me.registerZone(data)` reads as a deliberate bypass — most plausibly of the addon's remote-method surface, since `registerZone` is worker-callable — and mutating an inbound RPC payload to stop `resizeConfig` reaching the DragZone config application is a real decision, not a formality. The adjacent comment explains the *registry refresh* and is excellent; it does not cover either line. A maintainer a year out will not reconstruct why the dispatch is indirected, and the failure mode of "helpfully simplifying" it back to `me.registerZone(data)` is silent. Two clauses would fix it. Explicitly non-blocking — approval is terminal, so this is author's discretion.

**Second watch item (not a required action):** `Resize.apply()` clamps the low end to `0`, so live mode makes collapsing a sibling to zero extent interactively reachable and visible mid-gesture in a way deferred mode never was — you can now drag content to nothing and watch it happen. `#4723` is explicitly Out of Scope here and correctly so, but live mode raises that gap's value rather than leaving it flat. Worth a successor when the mode moves toward default, not now.

**Documented search:** I actively looked for (1) a geometry split-brain between main-thread inline styles and worker `wrapperStyle`, (2) proxy-mode regression from the new move-frame suppression, (3) leakage of the new `wrapperStyle` commit into `Neo.dashboard.DockSplitter`'s semantic-operation authority under ADR 0029, and (4) a vacuous AC-3 assertion that could pass without the resize having occurred. All four are closed — evidence in the audits below.
